title: [Transfrom] prevent transform from looping forever if delete by query fails permanently

timeline.message: call error handler if retention policy execution fails
timeline.author: Hendrik Muhs

timeline.message:
don't use epoch milli in dbq as epoch < 0 is undefined and can cause a
parsing error
timeline.author: Hendrik Muhs

timeline.body:
the yet unreleased retention policy feature uses delete by query to delete expired data. In
case of a failure its possible the indexer loops forever trying to finish a checkpoint. This
change has 2 parts: avoid the known misconfiguration that lead to the error, call the error 
handler if retention policy execution fails. This correctly connects the retention policy
execution to failure handling: A permanent error immediately sets the failed state, a
temporary issue enters the retry loop, only ending in failed state after a maximum number
of retries.

fixes #69274

Marking this as "non-issue", because retention policy is an unreleased feature, nevertheless this is a bug fix that should go into 7.12

Long max value - 1 = `9223372036854775806L` which, transforming from milliseconds to days is: 

106751991167.30064

`new TimeValue()` assumes that the value will be `ms`. I think this will cause flakiness.
Looks good other than my flaky test concern.

[nit] There is a slight inconsistency between wording of error messages:
"must be more than 60s"
vs
"must not be greater than"

Should there be some separation between "dbg Will"?
Maybe semicolon (";")?
